1. Harry is white. (Fact)  
2. Harry is blue.        (Licensed by Rule: “All white things are blue.”)  
3. Harry is quiet.       (Licensed by Rule: “All white, blue things are quiet.”)  
4. Harry is not young.     (Licensed by Rule: “If something is quiet and round then it is not young.”)  

ANSWER: True
reasoning:
We need to deduce whether "Harry is not young." We have initial facts:

- Harry is furry.
- Harry is kind.
- Harry is round.
- Harry is white.

Rules:

1. If something is round and not white then it is quiet.
2. All white, blue things are quiet. (i.e., if white and blue -> quiet)
3. Round things are kind. (But already kind)
4. All quiet, young things are round. (quiet & young -> round)
5. All white things are blue. (white -> blue)
6. If something is quiet and round then it is not young. (quiet & round -> not young)

Also: All quiet, young things are round is contrapositive? No, forward.

We need to see if we can derive "Harry is not young" via rule 6.

We must check if we can derive that Harry is quiet and round. We have round fact. We need quiet.

From rule 1: round & not white -> quiet. Harry is round but white, so not applicable.

Rule 2: white & blue -> quiet. Harry is white. But we need blue. We have rule 5: white -> blue. So from white we derive blue for Harry. So we have white & blue, thus quiet per rule 2.

Thus Harry is quiet and round. Rule 6: quiet & round -> not young. So we can derive Harry is not young.

We should confirm no contradictory facts like Harry is young. There is no fact saying Harry donc young. So we can conclude statement is true.

We must produce steps:

1. From fact: Harry is white. (given)
2. Rule 5: All white things are blue. => Harry is blue.
3. Rule 2: All white, blue things are quiet. Conditions: Harry white and blue => Harry quiet.
4. Rule 6: If something is quiet and round then it is not young. Conditions: Harry quiet and round (given). => Harry not young.

Thus statement follows.
